# 05 - Iteration ledger (generated by scripts/build_research_record.py)

Every iteration of every experiment, in order. 'params' = number of changed scalar parameters. The full hypothesis, operations and old/new values
are in `data/<experiment>/experiment_history.json` and `parameter_changes.json`.

### Hypotheses (as written before each edit)

* **iter001 - De-mean head weights (remove global-energy shortcut)**
  * Observed: Baseline head weights nearly all positive (mean +0.119, min -0.034); logit correlates r=+0.80 with image edge density vs only +0.34 for the label.
  * Hypothesis: Subtracting the mean head weight removes the direction that responds to overall feature energy, so predictions rely on which features differ, not how many fire.
  * Parameters: head.weight (512), head.bias (1)
  * Expected / risks: Lower train accuracy; val unpredictable (n=4); margin less tied to edge density. / May discard legitimate dog-leaning energy signal; could drop val accuracy.
* **iter002 - Negative conv2 biases to restore ReLU gating**
  * Observed: conv2 ReLU active on 95% of units, conv3 on 100%; network is almost linear.
  * Hypothesis: Setting each conv2 bias to minus the channel's mean pre-activation makes units fire only for above-average local evidence, adding selectivity.
  * Parameters: conv2.bias (32); head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: Sparser activations; cleaner separation if the evidence is above-average structure. / Mean-centering on 12 train images could encode them; zeroes weak channels.
* **iter003 - Negative conv3 biases to restore ReLU gating**
  * Observed: conv3 ReLU is 100% active; every conv3 channel contributes ~equally to dog_03.
  * Hypothesis: Centring conv3 pre-activations gates the final features so only distinctive regions contribute to the head.
  * Parameters: conv3.bias (32); head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: Higher feature variability across images; possibly clearer margins. / Sparse final features with only 12 head-fitting images could overfit.
* **iter004 - Wire the dead colour pathway into conv2**
  * Observed: conv2 weight magnitude from colour channels 12-15 is exactly 0.0 (vs 28.0 from edge channels); dogs are warmer on average (R-B 27.5 vs 13.4).
  * Hypothesis: Connecting the 4 colour-opponent channels to conv2 filters 24-31 lets warm/cool regional evidence reach the head.
  * Parameters: conv2.weight[24:32, 12:16] (72 values); head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: Possible gain if colour separates classes in unseen images; risk of dataset-specific colour correlation. / Colour may be a spurious cue (black cats, black dogs); may not generalise.
* **iter005 - Down-weight border cells of the head (background suppression)**
  * Observed: Mean |logit contribution| is 0.56 from the 4 centre cells vs 0.28 from the 12 border cells; cages/fences/grass dominate borders.
  * Hypothesis: Scaling border-cell head weights by 0.25 reduces reliance on background context.
  * Parameters: head.weight border-cell entries (384 of 512); head.bias
  * Expected / risks: Less background sensitivity; could lose pose/limb cues at borders. / Animals not centred lose signal.
* **iter006 - Break conv3 filter symmetry (filters 24-31)**
  * Observed: conv3 filters 24-31 produce identical outputs (max difference < 1e-6): 8 redundant channels, the head sums the same value 8 times.
  * Hypothesis: Giving each filter a different spatial kernel (vertical, horizontal, diagonals, left, right, top, bottom) makes them carry distinct spatial layout information.
  * Parameters: conv3.weight[24:32, 24:32] (576 values); head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: More informative final features. / Spatial kernels at a 16x16 map encode position, which may be arbitrary.
* **iter007 - Amplify colour pathway x3**
  * Observed: iter004 fixed dog_03 (warm dog) but colour weights (1/9 each) are small next to the edge weights; LOO accuracy did not move.
  * Hypothesis: Scaling the 72 colour weights by 3 raises colour influence; if colour truly separates classes, LOO and val should improve, otherwise it overfits.
  * Parameters: conv2.weight[24:32,12:16] (72); head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: Either more colour-driven corrections or new errors on black dogs/cats. / Colour is spurious in this tiny sample.
* **iter008 - Half-strength conv3 bias centring**
  * Observed: iter003 (full-strength) reduced LOO accuracy 0.875 -> 0.8125 on a model without the colour pathway.
  * Hypothesis: Half-strength centring keeps some gating without killing weak features.
  * Parameters: conv3.bias (32); head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: Gating benefit without LOO regression. / Interaction with iter004 colour features unknown.
* **iter009 - Centroid head rule (no variance scaling)**
  * Observed: LOO errors persist on dog_09 and dog_01 (dark/low-edge dogs).
  * Hypothesis: Using the plain class-mean difference is more robust and transfers better under LOO.
  * Parameters: head.weight (512), head.bias (1)
  * Expected / risks: Higher LOO accuracy if variance estimates were the noise source. / Ignores feature scale differences.

### Hypotheses (as written before each edit)

* **iter001 - Remove global-energy direction from the head (replication at scale)**
  * Observed: On train (n=1000) the baseline logit correlates r=+0.91 with image edge density but the label only +0.25; corr(logit,label)=0.26. Head weights are almost all positive.
  * Hypothesis: Subtracting the mean head weight removes the energy-following direction, so the logit depends on which features differ between classes. (Rejected on 4 val images in WSP-001; re-tested because 600 val images can now resolve a 1-point effect.)
  * Parameters: head.weight (512), head.bias (1) [closed-form head]
  * Expected / risks: Lower correlation of logit with edge density; val accuracy up if energy was a distractor. / May remove legitimate dog-leaning energy (dogs have slightly more edges: r=+0.25).
* **iter002 - Centre conv2 pre-activations with negative biases (replication)**
  * Observed: relu2 is 95% active and relu3 100%: ReLUs do not gate, so the network is nearly linear.
  * Hypothesis: conv2.bias_c = -mean(pre-activation_c over train) makes units fire only for above-average local evidence. (Accepted in WSP-001 on 16 images; re-tested at scale.)
  * Parameters: conv2.bias (32) + head refit (513) [bias is a data-derived constant; head closed-form]
  * Expected / risks: Sparser conv2 activations and more selective features. / Mean centring uses train statistics; can zero out weak channels.
* **iter003 - Centre conv3 pre-activations with negative biases (replication)**
  * Observed: relu3 is 100% active; every final feature contributes.
  * Hypothesis: Centring conv3 pre-activations gates the final features. (Rejected in WSP-001 on 16 images.)
  * Parameters: conv3.bias (32) + head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: More selective final descriptors. / Over-sparsification of final features.
* **iter004 - Wire the dead colour pathway into conv2 (replication)**
  * Observed: conv2 receives exactly 0.0 weight from the 4 colour channels. On this larger train set warmth barely relates to label (r=+0.08), unlike the 20-image WSP-001 sample.
  * Hypothesis: Connecting colour channels to conv2 filters 24-31 will NOT help (WSP-001's val gain was one image). This is a falsification test of the WSP-001 colour finding.
  * Parameters: conv2.weight[24:32,12:16] (72) + head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: No val improvement >=1 point; if one appears the WSP-001 finding replicates. / Spurious colour correlation on 600 val images is unlikely but possible.
* **iter005 - Suppress the bottom pooled row in the head**
  * Observed: Per-cell mean |effect size| on train: 0.43/0.42 for centre cells vs 0.10-0.20 for the bottom row (ground/floor/furniture), 0.22-0.37 elsewhere.
  * Hypothesis: Scaling bottom-row head weights by 0.25 reduces background noise.
  * Parameters: head.weight bottom-row entries (128 of 512), head.bias [closed-form head with mask]
  * Expected / risks: Small val gain; risk of losing legs/paw cues. / Animals whose lower body is informative.
* **iter006 - Identity routing for conv3 filters 24-31 (de-duplicate colour/blob features)**
  * Observed: After iter004, conv3 filters 24-31 each sum ALL eight conv2 blob/colour channels with the same kernel, so they are identical: colour evidence reaches the head as one feature repeated 8x (16 distinct values of 512).
  * Hypothesis: Routing conv3 filter 24+j to conv2 channel 24+j only gives eight distinct colour/blob descriptors, so the closed-form head can use them separately and val accuracy rises.
  * Parameters: conv3.weight[24:32] (8x32x3x3 = 2304 values) + head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: Val accuracy gain >=1 point if colour descriptors are individually informative. / Position-specific loss of the pooled colour sum; more head variance (more distinct features).
* **iter007 - Amplify colour pathway x3 (replication of WSP-001 iter007)**
  * Observed: iter004 (colour) was the only accepted edit; colour weights are 1/9 per tap vs edge weights up to 0.5.
  * Hypothesis: Scaling the 72 wired colour weights by 3 strengthens colour influence and raises val accuracy.
  * Parameters: conv2.weight[24:32,12:16] (72) + head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: Further gain if colour is genuinely informative; regression if it adds noise. / Overweights a noisy cue.
* **iter008 - Wire colour into conv2 corner filters 8-15**
  * Observed: Colour reaches conv3 only through the blob+edge path (filters 24-31).
  * Hypothesis: Adding colour-opponent input to the corner filters lets the network represent coloured corner/junction regions (e.g. nose, eyes against fur).
  * Parameters: conv2.weight[8:16,12:16] (72) + head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: Val gain >=1 point if colour-structure conjunctions matter. / Dilutes pure corner geometry.
* **iter009 - Coarser oriented edge filters in conv1 (wavelength 4 -> 6 px)**
  * Observed: The accepted model's logit still follows fine-scale edge density (baseline r=+0.91 with mean |dI/dx|, only +0.25 with the label). Fine 4-px Gabors mostly measure texture/JPEG detail.
  * Hypothesis: Replacing the 8 oriented filters with wavelength-6 px, sigma-2.0 Gabors lowers dependence on fine texture and raises val accuracy by >=1 point.
  * Parameters: conv1.weight[0:8] (8x3x5x5 = 600 values) + head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: Lower correlation with fine edge density, modest val gain. / Loses fine whisker/fur detail; 5x5 support truncates a 6-px wavelength.
* **iter010 - Centroid head rule (no per-feature variance scaling)**
  * Observed: Head has 512 features fitted from 1000 train images; centre-only edge features (96) match the full head on val (59.5 vs 60.7%), so many features add noise.
  * Hypothesis: The plain class-mean difference (centroid rule) is more robust and raises val accuracy by >=1 point. (Rejected in WSP-001 on 16 images.)
  * Parameters: head.weight (512), head.bias (1) [closed-form head]
  * Expected / risks: Higher val accuracy and CV accuracy if variance estimates were the noise source. / Ignores feature scale; may favour high-variance features.
* **iter011 - Scale border-cell head weights by 0.25**
  * Observed: Edge features restricted to the 4 centre cells reach val 59.5%, same as all 16 cells within noise (+-2%), with 4x fewer features.
  * Hypothesis: Down-weighting the 12 border cells to 0.25 reduces variance and background reliance.
  * Parameters: head.weight border-cell entries (384 of 512), head.bias [closed-form head with mask]
  * Expected / risks: Small val gain (~1 point). / Animal extremities near the border are lost.
* **iter012 - Prune the 8 weakest conv3 channels**
  * Observed: Head variance dominates: centre-only edge features (96) match all 512 on val. Per-channel mean |effect size| on train varies ~2x between channels.
  * Hypothesis: Zeroing the 8 conv3 filters (among 0-23) with the lowest mean |d| on TRAIN lowers head variance and raises val accuracy by >=1 point.
  * Parameters: conv3.weight rows for the 8 weakest channels (8x32x3x3 = 2304 values) + head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: Small val gain; CV roughly unchanged. / Selection uses train effect sizes (data-derived); may remove channels useful in combination.
* **iter013 - Average colour over a larger area (Gaussian sigma 1.5 -> 5x5 box)**
  * Observed: Colour wiring (iter004) was the only accepted edit (+3.5 pts val). Colour is a region property; conv1 colour filters are small Gaussians, exposed to JPEG chroma noise.
  * Hypothesis: A flat 5x5 box average of the colour-opponent signal yields a more reliable colour descriptor and a further >=1 point val gain.
  * Parameters: conv1.weight[12:16] (4x3x5x5 = 300 values) + head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: Modest additional gain from cleaner colour. / Blurs colour boundaries; box filter has hard edges.
* **iter014 - [round 2] Wire colour into conv2 parallel-pair filters 16-23**
  * Observed: Colour entered via the blob path (iter004, accepted) but not via corner filters (iter008, rejected).
  * Hypothesis: Giving the parallel-pair (stripe/texture) filters colour-opponent input adds colour-textured structure and raises val accuracy by >=1 point. Completes the colour-routing family.
  * Parameters: conv2.weight[16:24,12:16] (72) + head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: Small gain if stripe+colour conjunctions matter (e.g. fur patterns). / Same dilution that sank iter008.
* **iter015 - [round 2] Half-strength conv2 bias gating on the accepted model**
  * Observed: Full centring (iter002) moved val +0.7 pts but CV -0.5 pts: borderline, not rejected for harm.
  * Hypothesis: Half-strength centring keeps some selectivity without regressions and gives a >=1 point val gain.
  * Parameters: conv2.bias (32) + head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: Small gain. / Likely within noise.
* **iter016 - [round 2] Remove oriented-edge inputs from the colour/blob filters**
  * Observed: Blob+colour filters 24-31 carry gabor/9 edge input plus DoG plus colour; the edge part duplicates channels 0-23, and colour is the only modality with proven value.
  * Hypothesis: Zeroing the gabor taps (conv2.weight[24:32,0:8]) yields cleaner colour/DoG descriptors and raises val accuracy by >=1 point.
  * Parameters: conv2.weight[24:32,0:8] (8x8x3x3 = 576 values) + head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: Cleaner colour features; possible loss of edge-conditioned blobs. / Loses blob+edge conjunction.
* **iter017 - [round 3] Bright blob-pair detectors (eyes) in conv3 filters 25-28**
  * Observed: All earlier edits re-weighted generic edge/colour features; none encoded facial structure. conv3 filters 25-31 are still redundant duplicates of filter 24 (wasted capacity).
  * Hypothesis: Programming 4 conv3 filters as horizontal/vertical/diagonal pair detectors over the bright-blob channel (conv2 ch 24) gives the head a face-structure feature and lifts val accuracy by >=1 point.
  * Parameters: conv3.weight[25:29] (4x32x3x3 = 1152 values) + head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: Gain if eye pairs fall inside the pooled 3x3 neighbourhood at 16x16 (~8 px at 64x64). / Pair separation (8 px) may be too small/large for most images; 24 itself is an edge+blob+colour mix.
* **iter018 - [round 3] Dark blob-pair detectors (nostril/dark eyes) in conv3 filters 29-31**
  * Observed: Dogs' eyes and noses are dark blobs on lighter fur; the off-centre DoG channel (conv2 ch 25) is unused as a pair.
  * Hypothesis: Pair detectors over the dark-blob channel add the complementary face cue and raise val accuracy >=1 point.
  * Parameters: conv3.weight[29:32] (3x32x3x3 = 864 values) + head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: Gain if dark blob pairs separate dogs from cats. / Dark backgrounds create many spurious pairs.
* **iter019 - [round 3] Larger centre-surround blobs in conv1 (sigma 0.8 -> 1.5)**
  * Observed: The two small-scale DoG filters (sigma 0.8/1.6, ~3 px blobs) feed the blob+colour path; at 64x64 an eye or nose is a ~4-8 px blob.
  * Hypothesis: Matching DoG scale to part size (sigma 1.5/3.0) makes the blob channels respond to parts and raises val accuracy by >=1 point.
  * Parameters: conv1.weight[10:12] (2x3x5x5 = 150 values) + head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: Cleaner part-scale blob evidence. / 5x5 support truncates a sigma-3 surround; less fine detail.
* **iter020 - [round 4] Odd-phase (sine) Gabors in conv1: step-edge detectors**
  * Observed: conv1 oriented filters are cos-phase (even): they respond to thin bars, not to step edges such as body/ear/muzzle outlines against background.
  * Hypothesis: Replacing the 8 even Gabors with odd sine-phase Gabors (same wavelength 4, sigma 1.5) detects silhouette edges and raises val accuracy by >=1 point.
  * Parameters: conv1.weight[0:8] (600 values) + head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: Outline-driven features; may lose bar/whisker response. / Polarity-sensitive: ReLU keeps only one edge polarity per orientation (8 not 16 channels).
* **iter021 - [round 4] Sharper orientation tuning in conv2 line filters**
  * Observed: conv2 line filters 0-7 also take 0.5 weight from the two neighbouring orientation channels at the centre tap.
  * Hypothesis: Removing the neighbour taps makes each line channel orientation-specific and raises val accuracy by >=1 point.
  * Parameters: conv2.weight line-filter neighbour taps (16 values) + head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: More distinct line channels. / Noisier, less shift/rotation tolerance.
* **iter022 - [round 4] Half-strength conv3 bias gating on the accepted model**
  * Observed: relu3 is 100% active; full centring (iter003) regressed CV by 2.4 pts.
  * Hypothesis: Half-strength centring adds mild gating without the regression and raises val accuracy by >=1 point.
  * Parameters: conv3.bias (32) + head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: Small selectivity gain. / Likely within noise.
* **iter023 - [round 4] Hierarchy ablation: pass conv1 features straight through conv2/conv3**
  * Observed: 22 edits of every kind left val at 60-61%; the head (closed-form on 512 features) may be doing all the work.
  * Hypothesis: Replacing conv2/conv3 with identity routing of the 16 conv1 channels (256 informative features, 256 zero) gives accuracy within 1 point of the accepted model, i.e. the hierarchy adds nothing; if it *raises* val by >=1 point (fewer noisy features) it is accepted.
  * Parameters: conv2.weight (4608) + conv3.weight (9216) replaced + head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: Roughly equal accuracy (hierarchy decorative) or slightly better from lower head variance. / Loses the colour wiring's blob-path structure (colour reaches the head only through channels 12-15).
* **iter024 - [round 5] Multi-scale passthrough: 16 fine + 16 coarse conv1 feature maps**
  * Observed: iter023: the hand-composed hierarchy is decorative; the conv1 features + closed-form head give the same accuracy. So information lives in conv1 features, and 16 of 32 final channels were empty in iter023.
  * Hypothesis: Filling the 16 empty channels with 3x3-box (coarser) averages of the same conv1 features gives 512 informative features across two scales and lifts val accuracy by >=1 point over the accepted model.
  * Parameters: conv2.weight (4608) + conv3.weight (9216) replaced + head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: Higher accuracy if scale diversity helps; head variance rises with more distinct features. / Colour wiring from iter004 is dropped (colour enters only via channels 12-15 and their coarse copies).
* **iter025 - [round 6] Spatially shared head (32 effective weights)**
  * Observed: 24 extractor/head edits plateau at val ~60%, CV ~63%. The 512-feature head is fitted from only 1,000 images, and centre-only edge features (96) already match it: variance, not features, may be the limit.
  * Hypothesis: Sharing each channel's weight across all 16 cells (LDA over 32 cell-averaged features) cuts effective parameters 16x, lowers variance and raises val accuracy by >=1 point, at the cost of spatial layout.
  * Parameters: head.weight (512 tied to 32 values) + head.bias [closed-form head, rule lda_pooled]
  * Expected / risks: Higher CV and val if variance dominates; lower if spatial layout carries the signal. / Loses where-in-the-image information (centre vs border).
* **iter026 - [round 6] Centre/border shared head (64 effective weights)**
  * Observed: Per-cell effect sizes: centre cells ~0.43, borders 0.2-0.37 (train).
  * Hypothesis: LDA over 64 features (centre-cell mean, border-cell mean per channel) keeps the object-vs-background split with 8x fewer weights than the full head and raises val accuracy by >=1 point.
  * Parameters: head.weight (512 tied to 64 values) + head.bias [closed-form head, rule lda_pooled_cb]
  * Expected / risks: Best of both if variance and coarse layout matter. / Small gain, within noise.
* **iter027 - [round 6] Luminance-distribution (soft histogram) ramps replace the DoG blobs**
  * Observed: iter023/iter025/iter026: pooled low-level features plateau at CV ~63% whatever the head or hierarchy; the DoG channels 8-11 are the least informative conv1 group and encode only local contrast.
  * Hypothesis: Four thresholded single-pixel luminance ramps (bright 0.4, very bright 1.1, dark 0.4, very dark 1.1) pooled over the grid give soft histogram masses and raise val accuracy by >=1 point.
  * Parameters: conv1.weight[8:12] (300 values), conv1.bias[8:12] (4) + head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: Gain only if luminance distribution carries class information beyond edges and colour. / Label correlation with brightness is only +0.09 on train; likely noise.

### Hypotheses (as written before each edit)

* **iter001 - Wire the colour pathway into conv2 (replication at 8x data)**
  * Observed: WSP-003 baseline: train 0.602, val 0.601 (n=3000), 5-fold CV 0.601: all equal, so the model is bias-limited (features not rich enough), not variance-limited. conv2 receives 0.0 weight from the 4 colour channels.
  * Hypothesis: Wiring colour into conv2 blob filters 24-31 raises val accuracy by >=1 point. (WSP-002: +3.5 pts val on 600 images but 0 on the 2,000-image test; re-tested where a 1-pt effect is resolvable, n=3000.)
  * Parameters: conv2.weight[24:32,12:16] (72) + head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: Gain if colour is genuinely informative; none if the earlier gain was noise. / Spurious colour cue.
* **iter002 - Multi-scale passthrough: 16 fine + 16 coarse conv1 maps (replication at 8x data)**
  * Observed: WSP-003 baseline: train 0.602, val 0.601 (n=3000), 5-fold CV 0.601: all equal, so the model is bias-limited (features not rich enough), not variance-limited. WSP-002 iter024 reached CV 0.640 vs 0.632 (small data); the hierarchy ablation showed conv2/conv3 composition adds nothing over conv1 features.
  * Hypothesis: Filling all 32 final channels with informative fine+coarse conv1 features raises val accuracy by >=1 point; with 8,000 train images the 512-weight head can now use them without variance penalty.
  * Parameters: conv2.weight (4608) + conv3.weight (9216) replaced + head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: Gain if scale diversity helps. / Colour wiring dropped; no composition.
* **iter003 - Three-scale pyramid: fine blur + mid + coarse box**
  * Observed: Features are scale-limited: the head sees ~6 px (fine) and ~12 px (mid) structure only.
  * Hypothesis: Adding a coarse (3x3 box over the mid scale, ~12-24 px) channel set raises val accuracy by >=1 point.
  * Parameters: conv2.weight (4608) + conv3.weight (9216) replaced + head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: Gain if larger-scale structure carries class information. / Coarse averages blur into global statistics.
* **iter004 - Colour x texture conjunction detectors (thresholded soft-AND)**
  * Observed: On 8,000 train images: dogs have more of every channel (signed d>0), strongest for G-R (grass-green) and Y-B (tan/yellow) colour channels and near-horizontal edges; coarse copies of channels carry the same signal as fine ones (|d| 0.285 vs 0.284), so multi-scale added little. No ReLU ever gates: no feature can express a conjunction.
  * Hypothesis: 16 conjunction channels ReLU(colour/s_c + texture/s_t - 2) over {4 colour} x {horizontal, vertical, diagonal, blob} texture groups add genuinely new information and raise val accuracy by >=1 point. (Likely exploits scene context such as grass; that would be a context cue, not animal recognition.)
  * Parameters: conv2.weight+bias (4608+32), conv3.weight (9216) + head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: Gain if colour-texture co-occurrence is class-informative. / Scale normalisation uses train means (data-derived); scene-context shortcut.
* **iter005 - Fine conjunctions: every colour x every single orientation (32 channels)**
  * Observed: iter004 (grouped conjunctions + 16 passthrough channels): val +0.64, CV +1.00 vs the accepted model: conjunctions add real information but fall just under the 1-pt rule.
  * Hypothesis: Using all 32 channels for colour x single-orientation soft-ANDs gives a richer, non-redundant descriptor and raises val accuracy by >=1 point over the accepted model.
  * Parameters: conv2.weight+bias (4608+32), conv3.weight (9216) + head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: Larger gain than iter004 if orientation-specific colour co-occurrence is informative. / Loses marginal (passthrough) features and the DoG/blob channels; scene-context shortcut.
* **iter006 - Hue-bin and colour x blob conjunctions replace the weakest-orientation slots**
  * Observed: iter005 accepted (val 0.6357): colour x orientation conjunctions work. Orientations 3-5 had the lowest train |d| (0.16-0.18) so their 12 colour conjunctions are the weakest slots. Colour x colour (hue combinations such as yellow-green, orange) and colour x blob are untried conjunction types.
  * Hypothesis: Replacing those slots with 4 hue-bin ANDs (colour x colour) and 8 colour x DoG ANDs adds new information and raises val accuracy by >=1 point.
  * Parameters: conv2.weight rows for 12 slots (12x16x3x3 = 1728) + head refit (513); conv2.bias unchanged (-2.0)
  * Expected / risks: Gain if hue distribution / colour-blob co-occurrence is informative. / Hue bins capture scene colour (grass, indoor beige): context, not animal.
* **iter007 - Neighbourhood-tolerant conjunctions (colour at centre AND orientation over 3x3)**
  * Observed: iter005 accepted. Conjunction channels fire at 25-37% of positions (sensible gating). Colour (5x5 blurred) and Gabor responses are not pixel-aligned, and boundaries (fur vs background) put edge and colour in adjacent, not identical, cells.
  * Hypothesis: Averaging the orientation input over the 3x3 neighbourhood (misregistration tolerance) makes the conjunction fire for colour regions bounded by oriented edges and raises val accuracy by >=1 point.
  * Parameters: conv2.weight rows 0-31 (32x16x3x3 = 4608) + head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: Gain if boundary co-occurrence matters. / Blurs exact co-location information.
* **iter008 - Higher AND threshold (-2.0 -> -3.0): rarer, stronger co-occurrences**
  * Observed: Pre-activations are heavy-tailed (ch0 quantiles: 50%=-0.70, 70%=0.33, 90%=2.48, 99%=7.9); units are active 25-37% of the time.
  * Hypothesis: Requiring summed normalised evidence >= 3 isolates strong co-occurrences that are more class-specific and raises val accuracy by >=1 point. (One directional test, not a sweep.)
  * Parameters: conv2.bias (32) + head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: Sparser, more selective features. / Too sparse: low-variance features.
* **iter009 - Full-covariance LDA head (closed form) [data-fitted head, not a hand edit]**
  * Observed: train 0.629 / val 0.636 / CV 0.628 agree: bias-limited. The 512 pooled features are strongly correlated (fine/coarse and conjunction families), yet the head divides by per-feature variance only.
  * Hypothesis: w = (Sigma_within + 0.05*mean_var*I)^-1 (mu_dog - mu_cat), solved once from the 8,000 train images, raises val accuracy by >=1 point. Ridge fixed a priori, not tuned.
  * Parameters: head.weight (512), head.bias [closed-form head, rule lda_full]
  * Expected / risks: A clear gain if correlation structure is the bottleneck. / More of the accuracy comes from data fitting; 513 parameters estimated from 8,000 samples.
* **iter010 - [full-LDA head] 16 marginal passthrough + 16 grouped conjunction channels**
  * Observed: iter009: full-covariance LDA lifts val 0.636 -> 0.744 (train 0.752, CV 0.742): correlated features were the bottleneck, so redundancy no longer hurts and feature diversity may now pay off.
  * Hypothesis: Mixing 16 marginal passthrough channels with 16 grouped conjunctions (iter004 design) adds information the full-covariance head can exploit and raises val accuracy by >=1 point over 0.7443.
  * Parameters: conv2.weight+bias (4608+32), conv3.weight (9216) + head refit (513, lda_full)
  * Expected / risks: Gain if marginal features are complementary. / Loses 16 finer conjunctions.
* **iter011 - [full-LDA head] Multi-scale passthrough (16 fine + 16 coarse conv1 maps)**
  * Observed: Under the diagonal head multi-scale gave CV +0.9 pts but missed the rule; coarse copies were near duplicates (|d| 0.285 vs 0.284). A full-covariance head treats duplicates correctly.
  * Hypothesis: Fine + coarse passthrough exceeds the conjunction extractor (val 0.744) by >=1 point.
  * Parameters: conv2.weight (4608) + conv3.weight (9216) replaced + head refit (513, lda_full)
  * Expected / risks: Probably no gain (conjunctions add information that marginals lack). / Drops all conjunctions.
* **iter012 - [full-LDA head] Three-scale pyramid with a coarse box scale**
  * Observed: Same as iter011; features lack object-scale (20-40 px) structure.
  * Hypothesis: A coarse 3x3-box-of-mid scale adds larger-scale information and beats 0.744 by >=1 point.
  * Parameters: conv2.weight (4608) + conv3.weight (9216) replaced + head refit (513, lda_full)
  * Expected / risks: Probably no gain over conjunctions. / Drops conjunctions.
* **iter013 - [full-LDA head] Multi-scale passthrough with conv2.bias reset (valid re-run of iter011)**
  * Observed: iter011/iter012 collapsed to 50% because the edit left conv2.bias=-2.0 from the conjunction model: 384 of 512 features were exactly zero (debugged). Those two results are INVALID tests, not evidence.
  * Hypothesis: Fine + coarse passthrough (bias reset to 0) beats the conjunction extractor (val 0.744) by >=1 point.
  * Parameters: conv2.bias (32) reset, conv2.weight (4608), conv3.weight (9216) + head refit (513, lda_full)
  * Expected / risks: Probably below the conjunction extractor. / Drops all conjunctions.
* **iter014 - [full-LDA head] Three-scale pyramid with conv2.bias reset (valid re-run of iter012)**
  * Observed: Same bug as iter011 (stale -2.0 bias).
  * Hypothesis: Fine + mid + coarse features beat val 0.744 by >=1 point.
  * Parameters: conv2.bias (32) reset, conv2.weight (4608), conv3.weight (9216) + head refit (513, lda_full)
  * Expected / risks: Probably below the conjunction extractor. / Drops all conjunctions.
* **iter015 - [full-LDA head] Two spatial-frequency Gabor bands (odd orientations -> wavelength 6)**
  * Observed: Accepted model (iter013): val 0.766. Fine and coarse passthrough copies are near-duplicates (|d| 0.285 vs 0.284); a full-covariance head can use complementary features but gains nothing from copies.
  * Hypothesis: Moving 4 of the 8 orientations (1,3,5,7) to wavelength 6 gives 4 angles x 2 frequency bands, adds new texture information and raises val accuracy by >=1 point.
  * Parameters: conv1.weight[1,3,5,7] (4x3x5x5 = 300 values) + head refit (513, lda_full)
  * Expected / risks: Gain if texture frequency discriminates cat vs dog fur/background. / Halves angular resolution at each frequency; 5x5 support truncates wavelength 6.
* **iter016 - [full-LDA head] Local-peakiness channels replace the coarse marginal copies**
  * Observed: Fine + coarse passthrough (val 0.766) beats fine + conjunctions (0.718): scale contrast is exploitable by the full-covariance head. Coarse copies, however, are linear in the fine features before pooling, so they add only what a linear average adds.
  * Hypothesis: ReLU(f - 3x3 mean of f) per conv1 feature adds nonlinear local-contrast information not present in linear fine/coarse averages, and raises val accuracy by >=1 point over 0.7663.
  * Parameters: conv2.bias reset, conv2.weight (4608), conv3.weight (9216) + head refit (513, lda_full)
  * Expected / risks: Gain if texture/colour 'peakiness' is class-informative. / Loses the coarse marginals that currently help.
* **iter017 - [full-LDA head] Diagonal hue sectors replace the DoG blob filters**
  * Observed: Ablation (fit on train, val check): fine marginals alone reach val 0.765; dropping orientation filters costs 7.5 pts, colour 2.2 pts, DoG only 0.9 pts; colour alone reaches 0.677. Information is in the 16 conv1 filters, and the DoG group is the weakest.
  * Hypothesis: Replacing the 4 DoG filters with 4 diagonal hue-sector ramps (orange, yellow-green, blue-green, purple) doubles hue resolution (ReLU of a sum differs from the sum of ReLUs) and raises val accuracy >=1 point over 0.7663.
  * Parameters: conv1.weight[8:12] (4x3x5x5 = 300 values) + head refit (513, lda_full)
  * Expected / risks: Gain if hue resolution matters (grass, fur tones). / Loses ~0.9 pts of DoG blob information; hue may be a scene-context cue.
* **iter018 - [full-LDA head] Odd-phase Gabors replace the DoG blob filters**
  * Observed: Same ablation: orientation filters carry the most information (without them val 0.698; only them 0.733).
  * Hypothesis: Odd-phase partners at orientations 0,2,4,6 give quadrature phase information and raise val accuracy >=1 point over 0.7663.
  * Parameters: conv1.weight[8:12] (300 values) + head refit (513, lda_full)
  * Expected / risks: Gain if edge-vs-bar polarity is informative. / Loses DoG blob information.
* **iter019 - [full-LDA head] Combine local-peakiness channels (iter016) and odd-phase Gabors (iter018)**
  * Observed: iter016 (peaks) gave val +0.70 / CV +0.77 and iter018 (odd-phase Gabors) val +0.70 / CV +0.58, each just under the 1-pt rule and consistent across val and 8,000-image CV. They modify different layers.
  * Hypothesis: The two effects are additive: together they raise val accuracy by >=1 point over 0.7663.
  * Parameters: conv1.weight[8:12] (300) + conv2.bias (32) + conv2.weight (4608) + conv3.weight (9216) + head refit (513)
  * Expected / risks: About +1.4 pts if additive; less if they capture the same information. / Overlap; losing coarse marginals and DoG blobs.
* **iter020 - [round 2] Dark-bar polarity: negated Gabors replace the DoG blob filters**
  * Observed: Every even Gabor passes through a ReLU, so only the bright-bar half of its response survives; dark bars (dark fur against light background) are invisible. DoG and colour channels already have both polarities.
  * Hypothesis: Negated Gabors at orientations 0,2,4,6 recover dark-bar responses for the strongest orientations and raise val accuracy by >=1 point over 0.7663. (Sibling of iter018, which tried odd phase: +0.7.)
  * Parameters: conv1.weight[8:12] (300 values) + head refit (513, lda_full)
  * Expected / risks: Gain if dark-bar structure is informative. / Loses the DoG blob group (~0.9 pt).
* **iter021 - [round 2] Spend all channels on the 10 best conv1 maps x {fine, coarse, peak}**
  * Observed: Ablation: orientation filters 0,1,2,6,7 had the strongest |d|; weak ones (3,4,5) and the DoG group add little. Currently 32 channels = 16 maps x 2 types, including the weak maps.
  * Hypothesis: Using 30 channels as 10 strongest maps x 3 feature types (fine, 3x3 box, local peak) gives the full-covariance head more informative features and raises val accuracy by >=1 point.
  * Parameters: conv2.bias reset, conv2.weight (4608), conv3.weight (9216) + head refit (513, lda_full)
  * Expected / risks: Modest gain; risks losing information in the dropped 6 maps. / Selection of the 10 maps is ablation-informed (train fit, val check).

* **iter001 - Local-peakiness channels replace the coarse box copies (48 channels)**

  * Hypothesis: ReLU(f - 3x3 box mean of f) per conv1 map measures how much a feature stands out from its surroundings (nonlinear, not available linearly) and raises val accuracy by >=1 point over 0.7843. (WSP-003: peaks gave +0.7 on the 16-map net.)

  * Expected / risks: Gain if local peakiness is informative; fewer redundant features. / Loses coarse marginals (+0.3 pt).
* **iter002 - Soft-AND conjunction channels replace the coarse box copies (48 channels)**
  * Observed: WSP-004 baseline (hand-written 48-filter conv1, fine+coarse passthrough, full-covariance head): train 0.795, val 0.784, CV 0.777. Ablation: fine-only 0.781, coarse-only 0.778 (coarse copies add ~0.3 pt); odd Gabors most valuable (drop -> 0.768); coarse-freq Gabors, DoG, colour, hue each add <=0.4 pt. WSP-003: colour x orientation conjunctions were accepted under the diagonal head.
  * Hypothesis: 48 conjunction channels (4 colour axes x 8 even orientations, 8 corner pairs k/k+45deg, 8 odd-phase junction pairs k/k+90deg) add nonlinear information and raise val accuracy by >=1 point.
  * Parameters: conv2.weight+bias[48:96] (20,736+48) + head refit (1,537, lda_full)
  * Expected / risks: Gain if co-occurrence is informative. / Scale constants are train-derived; scene-context colour cues.
* **iter003 - Coarse-frequency ODD Gabors replace the weakest group (coarse even Gabors)**
  * Observed: WSP-004 baseline (hand-written 48-filter conv1, fine+coarse passthrough, full-covariance head): train 0.795, val 0.784, CV 0.777. Ablation: fine-only 0.781, coarse-only 0.778 (coarse copies add ~0.3 pt); odd Gabors most valuable (drop -> 0.768); coarse-freq Gabors, DoG, colour, hue each add <=0.4 pt. iter001/002 (nonlinear replacements of the coarse copies) both regressed.
  * Hypothesis: Replacing those 4 slots with coarse ODD-phase Gabors (orientations 0,2,4,6, wavelength 6) adds edge information and raises val accuracy by >=1 point over 0.7843.
  * Parameters: conv1.weight[44:48] (4x3x5x5 = 300) + head refit (1,537, lda_full)
  * Expected / risks: Gain if coarse step edges are informative. / Only 4 orientations at the coarse band.
